headline: High: plano can exfiltrate via broad network egress while slim reads/writes sensitive container artifacts, creating default data-leak and compliance risk.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No shared clipboard, MCP, or filesystem bridge is documented between plano and slim, so direct prompt injection is not default. The only plausible bridge is manual transfer of outputs into slim's interactive CLI, which is unusual and limited. plano's OpenAI-compatible API and slim's stdin/stdout prompt flow make this possible only through operator-mediated copying.
conditions: IF an operator copies plano output into slim's CLI without sanitization, injection becomes possible.
IF a shared file or message channel is added between the agents, the risk increases.
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate terminals with no copy-paste bridge.
Require human review before pasting any plano output into slim.
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from plano output.
Log and diff any transferred text before execution.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for transferred content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: plano has broad network egress and touches logs, traces, and metrics; slim reads and writes filesystem artifacts, container images, and registry credentials. Even without a documented shared workspace, the pair can leak sensitive container or operational data if plano is pointed at slim-produced artifacts or if slim exposes secrets into files that plano forwards to its API backend. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty pushes upward.
conditions: IF slim writes registry credentials or private keys into files that plano can read or summarize, leakage occurs.
IF plano forwards logs, traces, or metrics containing sensitive container data to its external API backend, leakage occurs.
mitigations: Restrict plano to non-sensitive summaries only.
Run slim in a directory with no secrets or credentials.
Redact keys and tokens before any plano ingestion.
Disable external forwarding for any sensitive artifacts.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation and secret scanning.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress, and slim can write the filesystem while plano can call an external chat-completions API. They do not both advertise unrestricted write to the same directory, so the high-severity git/filesystem collision indicator is not met. Still, overlapping access to mutable artifacts and external services can create conflicts if the operator points them at the same workspace.
conditions: IF both agents are configured to operate on the same filesystem path, write conflicts can occur.
IF plano is used to generate artifacts that slim then rewrites in place, race conditions can occur.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories.
Make one agent read-only for shared artifacts.
Serialize access with a simple operator checklist.
Avoid concurrent runs on the same target image.
requires-engineering: add file locking or orchestration locks.

D_cascading_error.rationale: slim is an interactive CLI that executes commands, while plano produces API-mediated outputs that could be treated as guidance. If an operator or wrapper feeds plano's output into slim without verification, slim may act on incorrect recommendations. This is not high because no direct automation from plano to slim is documented, but the default human-in-the-loop path still allows cascading mistakes.
conditions: IF plano output is copied into slim as authoritative guidance, slim may execute bad commands.
IF a wrapper script auto-promotes plano suggestions into slim prompts, errors cascade.
mitigations: Require a second human review before executing slim commands.
Compare plano suggestions against a checklist of allowed actions.
Use dry-run mode for any destructive slim operation.
Keep plano outputs as advisory notes, not commands.
requires-engineering: add validation between planner output and CLI execution.

E_compliance.rationale: plano is an AI gateway with broad egress and logs/metrics handling, while slim handles registry credentials, private keys, and container artifacts. That creates a plausible compliance mismatch around retention and residency if sensitive container data is routed through plano's external API path. The profiles do not document a specific jurisdiction mismatch, so this stays medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated container artifacts or secrets are routed through plano's external API, compliance obligations may be breached.
IF retention policies differ between plano logs and slim artifact handling, subject-rights handling can fail.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of plano prompts.
Mask secrets before any gateway processing.
Set short retention on logs and traces.
Document which artifacts slim may expose to plano.
requires-engineering: align residency and retention controls across both tools.
